context.root_cause: DETERMINISTIC HOST-ENVIRONMENT DEFECT (not transient worktree/venv state): Windows Python's subprocess.run(['bash','-c',cmd]) resolves 'bash' through the Windows PATH to the WSL launcher (C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe; 'where bash' order: C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\bash.exe, C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe, WindowsApps). Under WSL: (a) the Windows cwd C:\Users\...\t13 is mapped to /mnt/c/Users/.../t13, where the worktree metadata file (.git containing 'gitdir: C:/Users/.../.git/worktrees/t13') cannot be resolved - observed stderr: 'fatal: not a git repository: /mnt/c/Users/tw097/Desktop/261003_ai_test/table-queue/.worktrees/t13/C:/Users/tw097/Desktop/261003_ai_test/table-queue/.git/worktrees/t13' - so every block's 'root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)' fails and the block silently falls back to root=. (this is why block 01 'passed': it read the MAIN repo's .gitignore, which still carries the t25 lines); (b) the inherited POSIX-form PATH entries (/mingw64/bin, /c/Users/tw097/bin) are unusable in WSL, so 'uv' -> rc=127 (all 5 t26 blocks); (c) the driver's venv_abs = os.path.join(root, 'backend', '.venv', 'Scripts', 'python.exe') yields backslash form C:\Users\...\python.exe, which POSIX shells mangle via backslash-escaping (C:\Users\tw097 -> C:Userstw097) into a nonexistent relative name -> rc=127 (all 6 t29, all 6 t31, and the suite-running t35/t36 blocks whose captured summaries come back empty). Control experiment: invoking 'C:/Program Files/Git/usr/bin/bash.exe' explicitly from the same Windows Python with the same cwd gives PWD=C:/Users/.../t13, 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' = the worktree, /c/ mapping present, and the forward-slash venv path executes (Python 3.12.15).
